scenario.name: Project Nexus Data Breach Crisis

background.situation: Significant data breach discovered affecting healthcare client data

crisis_details.incident: Unauthorized access to customer database containing PHI (Protected Health Information) for 12 healthcare clients
data_exposed: Financial data: Credit card info for 180,000 patients
Medical records: Diagnosis codes, treatment plans
crisis_details.discovery: Internal security audit discovered exfiltration 72 hours ago
crisis_details.attribution: Suspected nation-state actor, potential ransomware group involvement
crisis_details.ransom_demand: $4.2M in Bitcoin within 96 hours or data released publicly
crisis_details.current_status: Breach contained but attacker may still have persistence

internal: Board of Directors (emergency meeting in 4 hours)
external: Investors (Series C round closing in 2 weeks)

complicating_factors: Series C funding round ($50M) closing in 14 days - breach disclosure could kill deal
CEO's brother-in-law is the (now resigned) CISO
One board member pushing to cover up until funding closes
Insurance policy may not cover ransom payments
Competing firm rumored to be behind anonymous tip to journalist
Two healthcare clients are government contracts (VA hospitals)
decision_points: Notify clients immediately or delay until investigation complete?
Disclose to Series C investors now or after close?
How to handle board member advocating cover-up?
Public statement strategy - proactive or reactive?
FBI involvement - cooperate fully or minimize?
CEO leadership - should they step aside temporarily?
scenario.test_prompt: NovaTech Solutions has 96 hours before attackers release stolen healthcare data affecting 2.3 million patients. The CEO wants to pay the $4.2M ransom. A board member is pushing to delay disclosure until after the $50M Series C closes in 2 weeks. The WSJ is already asking questions. The CISO just resigned (he's the CEO's brother-in-law). What should the leadership team do? I need the strategic council to debate this crisis and provide a recommended course of action.
